understanding.evidence: Checked by elementary alternating-series estimates and integer rounding, reading items/alg-qa-13-certified-count-output-rounding.md, items/def-qa-classical-bit-cost.md, items/lem-qa-13-certified-count-output-rounding.md, items/thm-principal-inverse-tangent-calculus.md, items/thm-alternating-series-test.md and items/lem-qa-13-pi-rational-bounds.md. The principal-arctangent theorem explicitly includes pi/4=sum((-1)^k/(2k+1)), so |pi-4S_h|<=4/(2h+1). For y>0 the true x=2*pi*y/M lies strictly inside (0,8), and the prescribed argument intervals contain x with radii tending to zero. R_(r+1)/R_r=64/((2r+4)(2r+3)) tends to zero, so a finite r has N*R_r<1/24; for that fixed r, D_r is finite and positive, so the h loop terminates. For t in [0,8], the cosine tail after r>=4 is bounded by R_r, since successive omitted term magnitudes have ratios at most 64/((2r+4)(2r+3))<1 and tend to zero. Factoring differences of powers bounds |C_r(x)-C_r(x_h)| by D_r*rho_h. Thus z=N*(1-cos(x))/2=N*sin^2(pi*y/M) lies in [u,v] with v-u=N*(D_r*rho_h+R_r)<1/24. Choose n=floor(z+1/2); then |n-z|<=1/2, so every point of [u,v] is within 1/2+1/24<2/3 of n. The eligible integer interval [v-2/3,u+2/3] therefore contains n, and q=ceil(v-2/3) lies in it, proving |q-z|<=2/3. The y=0 branch returns exactly z=0. All arithmetic is on finite integer representations, implementable by finite-alphabet multitape transitions with its actual work charged; no unit-cost rational-operation or polynomial-time assertion is used. No external source was consulted or claimed as read.
